subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers salvage the existing conflicting fork PR or authorize a narrow replacement fix for this issue?
rationale: The source-level bug is still present, but an open non-maintainer fork PR with closing syntax already owns the exact fix and cannot be updated by maintainers.

options.title: Authorize a narrow replacement
options.body: Open or queue a maintainer-editable replacement that covers current sync, async, and agent-tool title hydration paths, then supersede the conflicting fork PR.

options.title: Ask the fork author to rebase
options.body: Keep this issue paired to the existing fork PR and wait for the author to resolve conflicts and add current real-behavior proof.

options.title: Adopt the fork manually
options.body: A maintainer can cherry-pick the useful sanitizer/display-name changes into an OpenClaw branch and update them for current main.

recommendation.title: Authorize a narrow replacement
recommendation.body: Open or queue a maintainer-editable replacement that covers current sync, async, and agent-tool title hydration paths, then supersede the conflicting fork PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This login has the strongest available combination of merge, adjacent session-display, CODEOWNERS, and current-file history signals for choosing the branch path.
